stories.headline: Three keys for the Valkyries and Dream in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals
stories.summary: When Golden State and Atlanta play Thursday, a champion will be crowned or the WNBA Finals will be forced to Game 7.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- When the WNBA Finals resume Thursday, will we crown a champion or return to San Francisco for Game 7?

The Atlanta Dream host the Golden State Valkyries in a matinee Thursday (12:30 p.m. ET) at State Farm Arena in a must-win: Golden State leads the best-of-seven series 3-2 and looks to clinch the franchise's first WNBA championship in just its second season.

For the Dream, who have lost back-to-back games after taking a 2-1 lead, it's extend the season or watch the Valkyries celebrate a title on their floor.

If Atlanta wins, the series shifts back to the Valkyries' Chase Center and Ballhalla for a decisive Game 7 on Saturday.

But with so much at stake in Game 6, ESPN takes a look at how each team can win Thursday. And come back when Game 6 tips for live analysis, reaction and highlights from State Farm Arena.

Three keys for the Dream in Game 6

Avoid turnovers: Sounds easy, but it has been a struggle, particularly in the past two losses for Atlanta. In Game 4, the Dream had 18 turnovers that led to 16 points for Golden State. In Game 5, 17 Atlanta turnovers led to 21 points for the Valkyries. In short, that means Golden State has scored almost a quarter of its points off Atlanta turnovers in the two games. And in such low-scoring games, the Dream can't afford to allow the Valkyries to get that many points relatively easily.

"It's about playing at our pace, not getting sped up, making the extra pass," Dream forward Angel Reese said Wednesday. "My turnovers both games, I had offensive fouls. So I need to slow down a little and read the game better. I watched a lot of film ... so it's just kind of slowing down and getting to the spots that I know I can maximize."

Hitting open shots: This is another issue that might sound simple, but it hasn't been for the Dream, especially in the three losses.

In Game 1, Atlanta shot 33% from the floor and 16% from 3-point range. Those numbers were 33% and 17% in Game 4 and 29% and 23% in Game 5. Golden State's defense has been the biggest obstacle for Atlanta's offense, but the Valkyries aren't stopping everything. They're getting help from the Dream's shooting struggles.

Guard Allisha Gray has seen her shooting go from 46.3% (33.9% from 3) in the regular season to 34.4% (25.6% from 3) in her eight postseason games. Of course, she has been dealing with an injury to her shooting hand, suffered in Game 1 of the semifinals, which has impacted her scoring ability.

"The biggest thing is to just give myself grace," Gray said of dealing with the frustration of not being 100% during the Finals. "Shots I normally make, I may not make now. But I can't lose confidence in [myself], and I still have to find other ways to impact the game. I know I can play defense. I know I can hit layups."

Getting off to a fast start: Atlanta wants to feed off its crowd energy the way it did in Game 3, a 97-71 win on Oct. 21 in which the Dream looked the most themselves offensively. After that game, it seemed the momentum was with Atlanta, but that shifted in Game 4.

Reese said it matters plenty to get the State Farm crowd going early because the best way to crack the Golden State defense is to force the Valkyries to have to play catch-up basketball.

"We're here to get to our identity," she said of a team that averaged 91.3 points during the regular season. "I'm really trying to enjoy it.

"I haven't gotten enough steals. I need to make sure I get more steals, more deflections, more blocks -- that leads to my energy. And when we see a couple of shots going early, our confidence goes through the roof. When you get confidence early at home, that's what helped us get that 26-point win." -- Michael Voepel

Three keys for the Valkyries in Game 6

Continue strong pick-and-roll defense: Golden State has done everything well defensively in its three victories. One thing that has specifically stood out is how well the Valkyries have defended Atlanta in the pick-and-roll.

"A lot of times, it's tough to get the roll because they're doubling down," said Reese, adding the quality of her screens must be better.

Golden State center Kiah Stokes said the Valkyries take pride in being able to disrupt something that is a staple around the league.

"I think the key to pick-and-roll defense is if you can actually manage it 2-on-2 without requiring too much help," Stokes said. "Because that way, we can kind of stay [with] the shooters. Whereas, I'd say in [Game 5], I felt like maybe their guards were coming off a little too clean and getting open looks. So that was a personal thing for me."

The interesting thing is that even though Stokes didn't think Golden State's defense was as good as it could have been in Game 5, the Valkyries still held the Dream to a season-low 55 points. That should tell you how intense Golden State is on defense.

Win the rebounding battle -- or be close: Through five games, the Dream have outrebounded the Valkyries 189-178. Golden State has won the board battle twice: in Games 1 and 4, both victories. The Valkyries' biggest rebounding deficit was 44-33 in Game 5, but Golden State's overall defense was so good then that margin didn't come into play.

Golden State coach Natalie Nakase, though, targeted rebounding as an essential part of Game 6. And she sees that being just a general part of better execution from the Valkyries.

"Sometimes it's boring, but I like boring," Nakase said. "I like discipline. It's going to be kind of ugly and gritty, but that's how it's been all season long. We shouldn't be changing in the Finals."

Match the Dream's intensity level: This might be the hardest of all since Atlanta is in a must-win situation, and the Valkyries still have two chances to win this championship. But as much as they love playing at Ballhalla -- where Game 7 would be played Saturday night -- they don't want another game there this season.

Admittedly, from the outside it might seem anticlimactic to clinch a title on the road in what will still be the morning hours Pacific time on a Thursday. But the Valkyries aren't worried about any of that. They want to take care of business as soon as possible.

Stokes won three WNBA titles with Las Vegas, so she knows what it takes to close out a championship run. -- Voepel

"We have to understand Atlanta's mindset coming into the game," Stokes said. "For them, it is now or never. It's do-or-die. They're going to give it their all, their best fight. We have to be able to absorb that and still impose our will against them like we've done the last two games."

Come back at 12:30 ET for in-game analysis

stories.headline: Fantasy playbook: NFL Week 8 Shadow Reports, lineup locks and projected scores
stories.summary: An all-encompassing look at the matchups to exploit or avoid and lineup locks in fantasy, as well as projected scores for all NFL games.
stories.body:
Welcome to The Playbook for Week 8, which kicks off Thursday night with a game between the Panthers and Packers.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start advice, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule for the remainder of the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday after 1 p.m. ET.

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)

CAR-GB | BAL-BUF | TEN-CIN | ARI-DAL | MIN-DET | LV-NYJ | CLE-PIT

ATL-TB | IND-JAX | LAC-LAR | KC-DEN | NE-MIA | PHI-WAS | CHI-SEA

Carolina Panthers @ Green Bay Packers
Projected score: Packers 25, Panthers 22

Lineup locks: Chuba Hubbard, Josh Jacobs, Tetairoa McMillan, Matthew Golden, Christian Watson, Jalen Coker, Tucker Kraft

Fantasy Scoop: Jacobs made his 2026 debut on Sunday and was busy, playing on 35 snaps (54%) and totaling 11 carries and seven targets. The veteran back didn't do much on the ground (36 yards) but had the most productive receiving game of his career (5-55-1 on seven targets). It's hard to imagine Jacobs will be a consistent factor in the passing game as he totaled just 36 catches during both of his first two seasons in Green Bay and now has three career receiving TDs. Still, his rushing workload will only expand and he's always going to be a factor near the goal line (31 TDs in 33 games with the Packers).

Jacobs can be valued as a fringe RB1 in an excellent Week 8 matchup against a Carolina defense that sits top three in yards, TDs (nine) and fantasy points allowed to RBs. Backs are averaging a league-high 5.2 yards per carry against the Panthers.

Over/under: 46.7 (9th highest)

Win probability: Packers 58% (9th highest)

Baltimore Ravens @ Buffalo Bills
Projected score: Bills 33, Ravens 30

Lineup locks: Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry, James Cook III, Zay Flowers, DJ Moore

Fantasy Scoop: Henry remains a lineup lock despite falling short of 6.0 fantasy points in consecutive games for the first time since Weeks 10-11 of the 2023 season (while he was still with the Titans). Henry's very limited receiving role leads to the occasional dud -- he's been held under 12.0 fantasy points nine times in 24 games since the start of last season -- but that's more than offset by huge games thanks to his elite rushing and scoring ability (19-plus points in nine of those 24 outings).

Henry opened the 2026 season with 15.9-plus fantasy points in five consecutive games and, though his career-low 3.9 yards per carry is mildly concerning, he's a candidate for a leap forward with Jackson expected back under center. He's in an especially good spot this week against a Buffalo defense that sits dead last in EPA and that has allowed nine TDs (second most) and the third-most fantasy points to running backs. Buffalo has surrendered at least one RB score in all six games.

Over/under: 63.1 (Highest)

Win probability: Bills 58% (10th highest)

Tennessee Titans @ Cincinnati Bengals
Projected score: Bengals 29, Titans 14

Lineup locks: Joe Burrow, Chase Brown, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Carnell Tate

Fantasy Scoop: Tate is a strong bet for shadow coverage courtesy of DJ Turner II this week. On Sunday, Zay Flowers was able to produce the first game of over 15 fantasy points by a wide receiver against Cincinnati this season, but note that Flowers did nearly all of that damage while away from Turner's coverage -- he had one catch for 6 yards on 10 matchups with Turner.

Flowers (54% slot) benefits from a versatile role, whereas Tate (28% slot) will see Turner on nearly three-quarters of his routes. The 14 receivers Turner shadowed in 2025 averaged just 8.8 fantasy PPG and he's also limited Emeka Egbuka (11.3 points), DK Metcalf (12.1) and Parker Washington (2.0) already in 2026. Tate should be downgraded in what will be one of his toughest matchups of the season.

Over/under: 42.5 (11th highest)

Win probability: Bengals 94% (Highest)

Arizona Cardinals @ Dallas Cowboys
Projected score: Cowboys 33, Cardinals 21

Lineup locks: Javonte Williams, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Michael Wilson, Trey McBride

Fantasy Scoop: Dak Prescott's output has been a mixed bag thus far. He's delivered just two top-10 fantasy outings: a 29.8 effort against Washington in Week 2 and 23.3 points at Philadelphia on Monday night. Those two strong outings bookended a four-game stretch in which Prescott had as many interceptions (four) as he did passing TDs (exactly one in each of the four games). Prescott added some value with his legs early on (59 yards on 10 carries during his first three games), but that has dipped over the past four weeks (22 yards on six carries).

The good news is that Prescott is coming off a good game, leading a very fast-moving and pass-first offense, and is set up with a terrific Week 8 matchup against an Arizona defense that has allowed 19 total TDs and the second-most QB fantasy points. Prescott is a strong streaming option.

Over/under: 54.3 (2nd highest)

Win probability: Cowboys 86% (3rd highest)

Minnesota Vikings @ Detroit Lions
Projected score: Lions 26, Vikings 24

Lineup locks: Jahmyr Gibbs, Justin Jefferson, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta

Fantasy Scoop: T.J. Hockenson caught four out of five targets for 35 yards and one touchdown against the Colts on Sunday. It was yet another strong performance for the veteran tight end after he posted a 13-119-0 receiving line on 13 targets in his last full game with Kyler Murray under center (Miami, Week 4), though it's worth noting that Jefferson was sidelined for that game. Of course, even if we exclude that Week 4 game, Hockenson is handling a solid 20% target share, which has allowed a pair of 13.5-plus-point efforts.

Just like when he was in Arizona, Murray hasn't been shy about his attraction to throwing to tight ends, so Hockenson is very much back in the TE1 mix. That's especially the case this week against a Detroit defense that has allowed the most targets, catches, yardage, TDs (10!) and fantasy points to tight ends.

Over/under: 49.6 (4th highest)

Win probability: Lions 56% (13th highest)

Las Vegas Raiders @ New York Jets
Projected score: Jets 28, Raiders 26

Lineup locks: Ashton Jeanty, Breece Hall, Garrett Wilson, Brock Bowers

Fantasy Scoop: Geno Smith is fresh off a strong fantasy performance in which he completed 23 of his 30 passing attempts for 287 yards and three touchdowns. Smith took advantage of a shaky Miami pass defense, and, not coincidentally, his only other good fantasy outing of the season came in an even better matchup (26.0 points against Detroit in Week 3). Aside from those two games, however, Smith is averaging an ugly 11.1 fantasy points per game -- with four of those five outings coming against defenses ranked 21st or lower in QB fantasy PPG.

Although it's clear that Smith isn't close to being an every-week fantasy option, the good news is that he has another very good matchup this week. The Raiders have allowed the sixth-most passing TDs (16) and fifth-most QB fantasy points this season, with Justin Herbert (Week 2) the only QB who failed to reach 16.5 points against them. Smith's lack of rushing (22-42-0 this season) limits his output, but he's a terrific Week 8 streamer in a "revenge game" against Las Vegas.

Over/under: 53.2 (3rd highest)

Win probability: Jets 57% (12th highest)

Cleveland Browns @ Pittsburgh Steelers
Projected score: Steelers 23, Browns 16

Lineup locks: Jaylen Warren, DK Metcalf, Denzel Boston

Fantasy Scoop: Dylan Sampson was busy in his return from injury on Sunday. The second-year back played on 47% of offensive snaps, totaling 45 yards on six carries and 32 yards on three targets. Sampson is unlikely to see enough work for stand-alone fantasy value, but it appears he'll remain a thorn in the side of Quinshon Judkins' fantasy value. Judkins was limited to a season-low 51.5% snap share on Sunday and, while he was highly productive as a rusher (17-96-2), he was limited to a season-low one target (after averaging 4.0 in five games with Sampson sidelined).

Judkins has already been inconsistent (21-plus fantasy points in two games, but under 10 points in the other four) and is struggling with rushing efficiency (3.5 YPC), so Sampson taking on primary passing-down work is less than ideal. On the plus side, Judkins has handled 17-plus touches in five consecutive games and won't be short on carries and goal line work. Though he did put up 21.6 fantasy points against Pittsburgh in Week 4, Judkins is best valued as a fringe RB2 in this week's rematch. The Steelers have allowed only four TDs and 3.6 yards per carry to RBs this season.

Over/under: 39.2 (Lowest)

Win probability: Steelers 73% (7th highest)

Atlanta Falcons @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers
Projected score: Buccaneers 25, Falcons 23

Lineup locks: Bijan Robinson, Bucky Irving, Drake London, Emeka Egbuka

Fantasy Scoop: Michael Penix Jr.'s season is off to a terrific start, as the third-year QB sits ninth in QBR and has nine passing TDs to just one interception. Penix has thrown for at least 200 yards in all five games and now has exactly three passing TDs in two straight contests. Despite the strong play, Penix isn't yet on the starting radar in fantasy, with the main culprit being a lack of rushing output. Penix has a total of only 4 yards on 12 carries and now has 80 yards and a pair of scores on his 40 career rushing attempts. Annoyingly, Penix has actually lost fantasy points due to rushing in three out of five games this season.

Penix has cleared 20 fantasy points in consecutive games but was held below 15 points during his prior three outings and will thus be on the streaming radar only when the matchup is elite. That won't be the case this week against a Tampa Bay defense that has allowed the third-lowest EPA against the pass and the sixth-fewest QB fantasy points. No QB has reached 20 fantasy points against the Buccaneers this season.

Over/under: 48.6 (6th highest)

Win probability: Buccaneers 58% (11th highest)

Indianapolis Colts @ Jacksonville Jaguars
Projected score: Jaguars 29, Colts 19

Lineup locks: Trevor Lawrence, Bhayshul Tuten, Jonathan Taylor, Parker Washington, Tyler Warren

Fantasy Scoop: When we last saw the Jaguars (Week 6), Jakobi Meyers handled 10 targets, which matched his highest total in 16 games since joining the team midway through last season. Meyers turned the usage into a 5-83-0 receiving line. It was a solid outing, but it's just another "up" in what has been an up-and-down season. Meyers has reached 12 fantasy points in three games but has fallen short of 6.5 in the other three outings. He's seen eight-plus targets twice but has a total of 10 targets in the other four games.

Meyers' 15.6% target share is his lowest since he was a situational rookie in 2019 and, with so many mouths to feed in Jacksonville, that number may not rise much moving forward. The Colts have quietly allowed the fifth-fewest pass completions this season -- and only two receivers have reached 14.5 fantasy points against them (Zay Flowers, Carnell Tate). Meyers is best valued as a low-ceiling WR3/flex.

Over/under: 48.2 (8th highest)

Win probability: Jaguars 83% (4th highest)

Los Angeles Chargers @ Los Angeles Rams
Projected score: Rams 27, Chargers 13

Lineup locks: Kyren Williams, Puka Nacua

Fantasy Scoop: It's been a rough start to the 2026 season for top Chargers receiver Ladd McConkey, but it's worth noting that he's been productive when healthy. McConkey came out of the gate strong with a 5-82-1 receiving line on seven targets in Week 1 despite missing half of that game due to injury. He was limited to 45% of Los Angeles' offensive snaps the following week (3-35-0 on three targets) before rebounding with a 4-66-0 showing on five targets in Week 3 -- his only full game of the season thus far.

McConkey has totaled just 17 yards on three targets over his last two games, but he ran a grand total of 21 routes across the two games due to additional injuries. McConkey is expected to be healthy off the team's Week 7 bye and finds himself back in the WR3 discussion. He'll have his hands full this week against a Rams defense that has allowed the fewest catches and fifth-fewest fantasy points to WRs, though the Rams have surrendered eight touchdowns to the position (sixth most).

Over/under: 40.6 (13th highest)

Win probability: Rams 91% (2nd highest)

Kansas City Chiefs @ Denver Broncos
Projected score: Chiefs 21, Broncos 20

Lineup locks: Kenneth Walker III, Rashee Rice

Fantasy Scoop: Jonah Coleman returned from injury on Sunday and was an immediate contributor in the Denver backfield. The rookie paced Broncos running backs in snaps (28) and carries (nine), while also handling two targets on six routes. RJ Harvey (14 snaps, three carries, eight routes, two targets) scored the team's only touchdown and remained the top receiving back, whereas J.K. Dobbins (12 snaps, six carries, one route, zero targets) played a reduced role.

Coleman appears to be the Broncos' lead back -- he also had 13 touches for 58 yards and one TD in his lone pre-injury game back in Week 2 -- but Dobbins and especially Harvey figure to remain very involved in what is shaping up as a three-headed committee. Coleman is a low-ceiling flex this week against a Kansas City defense that has allowed 3.3 RB yards per carry (second lowest) this season. Granted Coleman didn't have a touch, but Denver RBs were held to 11.7 fantasy points when these teams met in Week 1.

Over/under: 40.6 (12th highest)

Win probability: Chiefs 54% (Lowest)

New England Patriots @ Miami Dolphins
Projected score: Patriots 29, Dolphins 20

Lineup locks: Drake Maye, Ollie Gordon II, A.J. Brown

Fantasy Scoop: Caleb Douglas returned from injury on Sunday and proceeded to score the first two touchdowns of his career. That's the good news. The bad news is that Douglas was limited to a mere three targets, which is the same number he saw in his most recent previous game (Week 2). Douglas totaled 19 yards and didn't find the end zone in that game. Douglas did post a healthy 5-94-0 receiving line on seven targets in his NFL debut (Week 1) and is no lower than second in line at receiver in Miami, but he'll of course need to see substantially more than three targets per game in order to find his way to the flex radar.

New England sits midpack in fantasy production allowed to receivers, but it's possible the Patriots choose to shadow Douglas with standout corner Christian Gonzalez. Douglas aligns on the boundary 80% of the time, so the rookie will be in jeopardy of a major dud if Gonzalez is assigned to him. For the time being, this is a situation to avoid.

Over/under: 48.9 (5th highest)

Win probability: Patriots 78% (6th highest)

Philadelphia Eagles @ Washington Commanders
Projected score: Commanders 27, Eagles 18

Lineup locks: Jayden Daniels, DeVonta Smith, Stefon Diggs

Fantasy Scoop: When we last saw the Commanders (Week 6), Terry McLaurin was lost for the season due to a knee injury. McLaurin's departure opens the door for the other Washington pass catchers to see more work, and TE Chig Okonkwo is certainly on that list. Okonkwo's season got off to a slow start due to injury, but he's now produced double-digit fantasy points in consecutive games. That includes a 4-60-0 receiving line on six targets in Week 5 and a 7-69-0 showing on seven targets in Week 6.

Okonkwo isn't yet a starting option, and we should temper expectations for a player yet to deliver a top-20 fantasy campaign, but he's a name to monitor in Washington's Daniels-led offense -- and with only the 32-year-old Diggs clearly ahead of him in target priority. At wide receiver, Treylon Burks and Antonio Williams are worthwhile bench fliers, with the rookie Williams offering the most upside.

Over/under: 45.1 (10th highest)

Win probability: Commanders 79% (5th highest)

Chicago Bears @ Seattle Seahawks
Projected score: Seahawks 26, Bears 22

Lineup locks: D'Andre Swift, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Luther Burden III, Colston Loveland

Fantasy Scoop: Caleb Williams is averaging 20.9 fantasy PPG this season -- and that number jumps to 25.3 if we exclude the slightly injured, shortened dud against Minnesota's elite defense in Week 2. Williams' season has included a 37.3-point, four-TD effort in Week 1, as well as a pair of games with 300-plus passing yards since his return from injury in Week 6.

Despite Williams' strong play, though, he's best left on benches in a brutal Week 8 matchup in Seattle. The Seahawks have allowed the fewest passing yards, a league-low 5.2 YPA and the second-fewest QB fantasy points. Their resume includes holding Drake Maye to 9.8 points, Bo Nix to 4.5 points and, most recently, Patrick Mahomes to 6.0 points.

Over/under: 48.4 (7th highest)

Win probability: Seahawks 65% (8th highest)

stories.headline: Who is this year's Mr. October? Tracking the playoff MVP for 2026
stories.summary: We go inside the numbers on the players who did the most to help their teams win this postseason.
stories.body:
Who was the hero of the 2026 MLB playoffs?

To try to answer to that question, we tabulated the cumulative win probability added figures for every player in the postseason. But this year we added a twist: The deeper we got into the playoffs, the more weight the WPA carried. The division series counted double the wild-card round, then we doubled it again for the championship series and, finally, once again for the World Series.

After all that, Milwaukee Brewers reliever Aaron Ashby lapped the field. He wasn't named MVP of the World Series but if there was an overall playoff MVP -- which there should be -- Ashby would have been in the running.

His 18 shutout innings were the foundation of Milwaukee's stifling championship-level run prevention during its title run.

World Series Game 5 hero: After a grueling, 12-inning Game 4, the Brewers really needed Jacob Misiorowski to be their Game 5 hero. He came through. Misiorowski threw 5 ⅔ scoreless innings, shrinking the load for the tired bullpen behind him and making sure they had a lead to protect. Misiorowski didn't blow away the Tampa Bay Rays, but we're not talking a sore-armed Dizzy Dean in the 1938 World Series here. He wasn't getting by on guile alone, but lightning stuff he flashed until a leg issue forced him from the game. Long after, when manager Pat Murphy finally got to the media conference room, he said, "I got news for you, he's not even scratching the surface of how good (he) can be." Be afraid, hitters. Be very afraid.

Methodology
As mentioned above, each player's win probability added (WPA) is tracked on a per-game basis. Each round of the playoffs counts double that of the previous round. The tabulation is then converted to an AXE-style index in which 100 represents the average for all postseason players. The "Change" column looks in the changes in AXE numbers from the previous day for players who were in action. You can sort this column by clicking on it to see the day's heroes.

stories.headline: Xabi Alonso: Estêvão will 'have his moment' at Chelsea
stories.summary: Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso insists Estêvão will have "his moment" this season, with the teenage winger having only played 172 minutes.
stories.body:
Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso insists Estêvão will have "his moment" this season, with the teenage winger having only played 172 minutes.

Estêvão, 19, has started in just two games under head coach Xabi Alonso and was an unused substitute in Chelsea's defeat on penalties to Liverpool in Wednesday's Carabao Cup quarterfinal.

"I understand his situation and that he could be happier for sure," Xabi Alonso said in a post-match news conference when asked about the Brazil international's limited playing time.

"Every player wants to play, wants to be part of the team. We have had some intense games and there will be moments for everything. I'm sure Este [Estêvão] will have his moment. It's my responsibility and we need to deal with that."

Estêvão, who missed the 2026 World Cup through a hamstring injury, made 12 Premier League starts last season and had eight goals in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior.

- Liverpool beat Chelsea in shootout to reach Carabao Cup quarters

- Is it too soon for Chelsea to regret getting rid of Aston Villa's Nicolas Jackson?

- Xabi Alonso on João Pedro's Chelsea absence: Looking for solutions, not excuses

Chelsea are back in action on Saturday when they host beleaguered Manchester United in the Premier League.

stories.headline: Debunk or double down? Judging 10 early-season NBA overreactions
stories.summary: A 29-year-old is the NBA's next breakout star. Miami's Giannis era is already cooked. And so are the Thunder, Knicks and Warriors. Which overreactions are valid?
stories.body:
Welcome to the final days of October, featuring falling leaves, early sunsets, Halloween decorations illuminating the night -- and the yearly pastime of overreacting to the first week of a new NBA season.

After all, small sample size theatre has provided early gems such as:

The sky is falling in Oklahoma City, New York and Miami!

The three-guard experiment in San Antonio needs to go!

Charlotte is already better without LaMelo Ball!

Ty Jerome? Ty Jerome!

With those early storylines and more in mind, let's examine 10 popular overreactions to the young 2026-27 season -- and determine which have staying power. (Note: stats through Tuesday's games.)

The Miami Heat will finish with their worst record since 2008.
Zach Kram: Not an overreaction

For reference, 2007-08 was the last time the Heat finished with fewer than 37 wins, the season that they tanked down the stretch to go 15-67 in a futile attempt to land Derrick Rose in the draft.

Merely by the law of averages, the 2026-27 Heat are bound to improve. They've had the seventh-worst shooting luck on offense, according to GeniusIQ tracking, and the second-worst shooting luck on defense. Miami is actually forcing teams into tough shots, but its opponents have been on fire regardless, making 53% of their midrange shots and 40% of their 3s, per Cleaning the Glass.

On the other hand, the Heat's offense has been stuck in the mud even accounting for that poor shooting luck, and guard Davion Mitchell is the only role player who looks comfortable playing with Giannis Antetokounmpo. There's time for that to change -- but as of Wednesday, ESPN's Basketball Power Index predicts the Heat will finish the season with just 38 wins. That's already down from 46 projected wins in the preseason, and just one ahead of this historical franchise benchmark.

Ben Golliver: Overreaction

Let's be clear: The Antetokounmpo era in South Beach is off to an atrocious start. Instead of building off its blockbuster trade for the two-time MVP with a transformative offseason, the Heat lost Norman Powell to the Chicago Bulls in free agency and settled for adding Klay Thompson, who is a shell of his former self at age 36. On the court, it's already clear that the Heat need another proven ball handler and more shooting, and Antetokounmpo needs more time to jell with Bam Adebayo.

Despite all those challenges, it's reasonable to give Heat coach Erik Spoelstra and his staff a long runway. Antetokounmpo's need to dominate the ball has clashed with the free-flowing offensive system that Miami utilized in 2025-26, and several veteran players seem to be easing into the new season. Spoelstra is a tinkerer who has conjured winning records from less talented rosters, and he'll be willing to trust his younger options if Miami's offensive struggles persist.

It's probably best to withhold judgment until after the Heat's upcoming trip out West. If the Heat can't get right against teams such as the LA Clippers, Sacramento Kings, Golden State Warriors and Utah Jazz, sound the alarm. There is some good news: Antetokounmpo has been productive in Miami's three defeats, averaging 28.5 points, 9.5 rebounds and 5.0 assists after missing most of last season due to injuries.

The Oklahoma City Thunder's title hopes are gone without Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace.
Kram: Not an overreaction

Earlier this week, I went into more depth about the impact of these two long-term injuries on Oklahoma City's title chances. The simplified version: The Thunder's winning formula over the past few seasons has been to combine MVP-level offense from Gilgeous-Alexander with the best defense in the league. The collective loss of Williams, Wallace and Luguentz Dort (via summer trade) bends that second factor out of shape.

Yes, centers Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein still form an imposing backline, and Alex Caruso (currently out with an ankle sprain) remains a singular defensive force. But the rest of Oklahoma City's perimeter rotation is now so thin, with enough defensive questions, that I would be surprised if it won another title -- barring a return from one of those injured starters before the playoffs or a significant in-season trade.

Golliver: (emotional) overreaction

Yes, it sure felt as if the sky was falling Monday when Thunder general manager Sam Presti announced that Williams and Wallace are out for the foreseeable future with significant injuries. That's no way to launch a title chase. After those injuries and the offseason trades of Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe, the Thunder are down five of their top six players by minutes logged during the 2024-25 championship season. Oof.

But there's an awful lot of talent remaining around Gilgeous-Alexander, who has been sensational to start this season. Oklahoma City showed its resolve by beating Phoenix on Monday night, and it's worth noting it was only one win from reaching the Finals last year despite an injury-plagued season and postseason for Williams. Presti has picks and tradeable contracts to invest in stop-gap additions before the trade deadline, but he also has a deep roster that was built for the long haul. Count out the Thunder at your own peril.

Ty Jerome will be an All-Star.
Golliver: Overreaction

Only a jerk would root against Jerome, who looks destined for a career year after surviving countless fits and starts to get here. But the Memphis Grizzlies' schedule has been about as soft as it gets to start the season: The Jazz look poised to give up 30 points to any opposing guard, while the Warriors' injury issues and the Kings' general dysfunction disqualify them from being quality wins. Jerome is a talented scorer who more than earned this promotion to lead ball handler, but let's check back in a few weeks. The good news: LeBron James and Kawhi Leonard left the Western Conference over the summer, so there are more available All-Star spots than usual.

Kram: Not an overreaction

Jerome wasn't an All-Star last season, of course, because he played only 15 games. But he has been a star-level offensive player for a while now, even if few people recognized it until he started averaging 30 points. Here are the NBA's leaders in offensive box plus-minus for the 2025-26 campaign:

Nikola Jokic
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
Ty Jerome
Luka Doncic
Giannis Antetokounmpo
Kawhi Leonard
Victor Wembanyama
Stephen Curry
Jamal Murray
Donovan Mitchell

It doesn't matter when Jimmy Butler III returns -- the Golden State Warriors are cooked.
Golliver: Not an overreaction

The Warriors finally got their first win of the season Monday, but their opening week has been disheartening. With Butler, Kristaps Porzingis and several players missing time with injuries or ailments, the Warriors sat Curry on a back-to-back and rolled out a starting lineup featuring Yaxel Lendeborg, Brandon Williams, Will Richard, Gui Santos and Graham Ike on Saturday against the Phoenix Suns. That five-man group -- great fodder for Charles Barkley on "Who he play for?" -- will combine to earn less than $20 million this season.

Meanwhile, Butler ($56 million) and Porzingis ($19.5 million) are missing in action. There's no way to overcome that math.

Kram: Not an overreaction

We finally agree, Ben. I'm not especially surprised by the Warriors' predicament because this seemed like a gap year from the start, due to all their injury issues and the lack of any real upgrades over the summer. (Aside from Lendeborg, who looks incredible as a rookie.)

Maybe they can stick around the play-in race because the West looks shallower than usual -- the Jazz might also be cooked if Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. are out for a while -- but Golden State's most important goal should be setting itself up for greater success in 2027-28.

The San Antonio Spurs will kill their three-guard starting lineup by Thanksgiving.
Kram: Overreaction

I tend to think debates about starting lineups are overblown because of how much teams mix and match over the course of a game; lo and behold, the guard trio of De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle has shared the court for just 43 minutes across four games this season.

And while it's way too early to come to significant conclusions using net rating, it's not as if the Spurs have struggled in those minutes. They're plus-15.4 with that three-guard lineup, according to databallr. If San Antonio's coaching staff believes it needs to keep Fox, Harper and Castle in the starting lineup for intangible reasons, then there's no evidence yet that that's a bad idea.

Golliver: Overreaction

Spurs coach Mitch Johnson could be headed for a real saga that might take months to play out. Of course, the critical decision is whether to start Fox, Harper or both point guards. But Johnson could also buy time for that duo to work things out by swapping Devin Vassell for Tobias Harris or Julian Champagnie. Given Fox's enormous salary and Harper's potential, San Antonio must exhaust every possibility before shifting one guard to the bench.

Sacramento Kings coach Doug Christie won't make it to the new year.
Golliver: Not an overreaction

There are so many red flags coming out of Sacramento that it's starting to look like an Olympics opening ceremony. Naturally, the central tension concerns rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. and veterans Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine. The Kings have turned Acuff loose for 93(!) shots in his first four career games with hopes he will develop into a franchise guard, but his more experienced teammates have good reason to wonder whether that's the best approach to winning.

Christie is stuck, and Ben Simmons' preseason Achilles tear made a tough job even tougher. The Kings look destined to be the NBA's worst team, and that level of ineptitude typically prompts a response from owner Vivek Ranadivé.

Kram: Not an overreaction

The Kings have let go of five coaches since Ranadivé bought the team in 2013. Two firings came at the end of a season (George Karl in 2016 and Dave Joerger in 2019), but the other three came early in a campaign: Luke Walton (2021) in November and Michael Malone (2014) and Mike Brown (2024) in December.

That pattern tells me there's greater than a 50% chance that Christie won't make it to 2027.

The New York Knicks won't get out of the first round.
Kram: Overreaction

I predicted before the season that New York would win fewer regular-season games than a year ago, so I can't profess to be surprised by their sub-.500 start against a tough schedule.

The greatest on-court problem for the Knicks is their 25th-ranked offense, but I expect a prompt turnaround: They rank last in making just 30% of their midrange shots, per Cleaning the Glass, after ranking fifth at 45% with largely the same roster a year ago.

In looking ahead to the postseason, moreover, I would have to see a much larger sample of struggles to consider the likelihood that New York won't be favored in any playoff matchup in the East. The competition will be tougher this year, but the Knicks are proven playoff performers.

Golliver: Not an overreaction

This one is more about vibes than hard analytics. As is often the case for defending champions, the Knicks have had a challenging opening week schedule filled with marquee opponents. In that context, the 1-3 start really isn't the end of the world. New York was in competitive games against aspiring contenders in the 76ers and Celtics last week and then handed the Detroit Pistons their first loss on Tuesday.

But the Knicks' inability to pull out those close games was a reminder of just how charmed their 2026 postseason was from start to finish. Jalen Brunson seemingly hit every big shot he needed to hit, and the one time Brunson didn't come through, OG Anunoby was right there for the one-in-a-million tip-in.

Time after time, the Knicks cheated death with second-half comebacks. That doesn't feel like a sustainable formula now that they've got the target on their backs. Owner James Dolan has also operated like a man who is comfortable with one ring rather than desperate to add another.

Trying to win back-to-back championships has exhausted younger teams than the Knicks in recent years, so no one should be all that surprised if they run out of gas or encounter season-altering injuries before May.

Offseason trades made the Charlotte Hornets' current roster better.
Kram: Not an overreaction (although I'm prepared for Ball to make this statement look silly)

We all thought Charlotte's surprising offseason trades were made with an eye toward the future. After all, the franchise dealt two foundational players and their two highest-salaried players in Ball and Miles Bridges. But the Hornets received so much flexibility and so many valuable draft assets in return that the "one step back, two steps forward" approach made sense.

We might have been giving the Hornets' present-day roster short shrift with that assessment. Charlotte has a winning record despite receiving zero minutes from its starting backcourt, as Coby White and Kon Knueppel deal with injuries. Brandon Miller appears to have taken a leap after signing a five-year rookie extension. And offseason additions Naz Reid and Grayson Allen, who came to Charlotte as part of the Ball and Bridges trades, have combined to average 36.3 points while making 44% of their 3-pointers. Reid, in particular, represents a meaningful upgrade over Bridges at power forward.

Golliver: Overreaction

The jury is still out on the Hornets given the injuries you mentioned and their weak quality of competition to date. With that said, the decision to trade Bridges is already shaping up to be one of those moves they will never regret.

Charlotte's short-term success will be determined by Miller's ability to consistently flex his muscles as an alpha scorer and Knueppel's comfort handling greater playmaking duties. Beyond that, Hornets ownership must demonstrate a willingness to spend to build around that budding duo.

The Ball trade could wind up as a win-win for Charlotte and Minnesota, but at some point, the Hornets will need to prioritize talent acquisition and retention rather than careful cap management. Otherwise, they're spinning their wheels.

Walker Kessler should be on Team USA in 2028.
Golliver: Not an overreaction

Before the season, the Lakers argued that Kessler was worth paying a premium price in draft picks in their summer sign-and-trade with the Jazz because it's incredibly difficult to find centers at his age (25) with the ability to finish plays on offense and credibly protect the paint on defense.

Grant Hill, Spoelstra and USA Basketball would be wise to target big men with that exact skill set for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, especially if Joel Embiid, Anthony Davis and James opt not to return after winning gold in Paris. Adebayo, Holmgren, Jackson and Evan Mobley could all be in the mix, but Kessler brings a level of sheer size and physicality that those players lack. Wouldn't it be helpful to have a traditional center to deploy with Wembanyama and Jokic looming as threats to the U.S. dynasty?

Kram: Overreaction

You cited the Grizzlies' schedule when cautioning about Jerome's hot start. I'll do the same for Kessler, whose two big games to date came against a Warriors team that didn't start a center and a Clippers team with Isaiah Jackson in the middle. That's not exactly Wembanyama- and Jokic-level competition.

Kessler does have international experience, as he was a deep reserve for the unsuccessful 2023 World Cup squad. I believe he's on the long list of American big men for 2028, but I would need much more evidence to place him higher in the pecking order.

The Chicago Bulls will be the worst team in the East.
Golliver: Not an overreaction

For all the preseason talk about improved parity this season thanks to the new lottery rules, there are still some pretty bad teams. The Bulls, Bucks and Nets have all looked like viable contenders to finish with the conference's worst record. (And yet, somehow, the Heat have been harder to watch than all of them.)

The scary part about Chicago's start is how thoroughly Toronto and Boston thumped the Bulls. While the Bulls want to play fast under new coach Tiago Splitter, they're just getting completely run off the court by good teams.

There's obviously no reason to panic if the blowout losses mount: Caleb Wilson should be encouraged to play free and make mistakes, and Chicago's new front office should focus on which of its veteran players look like long-term fits around the promising rookie forward. And is it too early to predict the Bulls will be getting rid of players at the trade deadline?

Kram: Overreaction

The Bulls rank dead last in offensive efficiency, but I believe that's more a product of bad luck than bad process. According to GeniusIQ tracking, the Bulls rank fourth in quantified shot probability, which accounts for factors such as location, defender distance and shooter talent. But the Bulls have underperformed that shot quality by 11.1%, which ranks last by a mile. For context, the largest gap for any team over the full 2025-26 season was just 1.7% -- so Chicago's shotmaking is bound to improve.

That doesn't mean I think the Bulls will reach the play-in tournament or anything so lofty. But I do believe that they'll play more like a typical rebuilding team going forward, rather than losing every other game by blowout margins.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: What to watch in Canadiens-Stars, 10 other Thursday games
stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
Thursday marks one month since Opening Night of the 2026-27 NHL season, which has produced quite a lot of hot takes and overreactions. Go here to read Greg Wyshynski's appraisal of the juiciest.

And the games continue, including 11 of them for hockey fans to ingest tonight.

Here's a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Winnipeg Jets at Tampa Bay Lightning

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TB -238, O/U: 5.5

Generally speaking, jets and lightning don't mix. And given the Winnipeg Jets' current tailspin -- six straight losses -- this doesn't seem to be a great time to be visiting the hockey team that plays in Central Florida.

The Lightning are undefeated at home this season, but are banged up with both Brandon Hagel and Victor Hedman listed as day-to-day.

Utah Mammoth at Pittsburgh Penguins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -130, O/U: 6.5

Just 10 days after squaring off in Salt Lake City -- a 5-4 win for the home Mammoth -- these two clubs will battle again in the Steel City.

Any time Logan Cooley plays in Pittsburgh, we are contractually obligated to point out that he got his start in Sidney Crosby's "Little Penguins" program. Cooley has six points in six career games against the Pens, including an assist in Utah's win this season.

The Penguins have a long list of players on the injury report that could return Thursday, including Evgeni Malkin, Ben Kindel, Egor Chinakhov and Samuel Girard.

Columbus Blue Jackets at Carolina Hurricanes

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CAR -218, O/U: 6.5

After a rough start, the Blue Jackets have been better of late, with three wins (all in OT) in their last five games. Can they keep the magic rolling against the Canes?

Carolina has been rolling all season, including 10 wins in their past dozen games. Goaltender Pyotr Kochetkov has been particularly strong, with an 8-0-0 record, 1.62 goals-against average and .918 save percentage.

Chicago Blackhawks at Detroit Red Wings

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+/Disney+/Hulu) | DET -180, O/U: 6.5

This game is a continuation of one of the NHL's most storied rivalries, having begun in 1926-27. The teams have met 838 times; Detroit holds the edge in the regular season with a 378-278-84-17 record, while Chicago has a 43-38 advantage in the playoffs.

At this point, it's a long shot that either team makes the 2027 playoffs, but this game has a number of fascinating elements.

Patrick Kane will be returning to the team for which he skated the past three seasons, and teammate Connor Bedard has found success against Detroit; he has six points in five career games vs. the Red Wings, including a goal and two assists Nov. 9 of last season.

Detroit's leading scorer, Alex DeBrincat, has had even more success against Chicago, with 11 points in eight career games against his former team.

And we can't forget that this pairing of teams is easily one of the best uniform matchups possible in the NHL.

Boston Bruins at St. Louis Blues

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | STL -115, O/U: 5.5

It's a 2019 Stanley Cup Final rematch! The rosters have changed quite a bit since then, but key contributors remain on each roster.

The B's are off to a considerably better start in the standings; their 9-3-1 record has them atop the Atlantic, while the Blues (5-6-1) are sixth in the Central. And at least on paper, it appears that the Bruins are better at scoring goals (3.77 per game vs. 2.92 for the Blues) and preventing them (2.15 per game vs. 3.08). But this Blues team can surprise, including a 6-2 win over the defending Western Conference champ Golden Knights a week ago.

Washington Capitals at Nashville Predators

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | WSH -112, O/U: 6.5

As it's his last season in the NHL, this will also be Alex Ovechkin's final appearance in Smashville. He's scored 20 goals against the Preds in 31 career games, including seven in the last 10. Will he get another Thursday?

Another future Hockey Hall of Famer plays for the home team in this one, and Steven Stamkos is scoring ahead of a point-per-game pace this season, with 15 through 12.

Montreal Canadiens at Dallas Stars

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -162, O/U: 5.5

In the marquee matchup of the night, a Stanley Cup hopeful backstopped by a 21-year-old American goalie visits another Stanley Cup hopeful backstopped by a 27-year-old American goalie. It's unclear if we'll get Jacob Fowler vs. Jake Oettinger in this one, but both have been superb this season.

The superstars up front have delivered too; Lane Hutson and Cole Caufield are just behind the injured Nick Suzuki on the Habs' scoring leaderboard, while Mikko Rantanen is delivering the goods for Dallas.

Stathletes does not project this matchup to be particularly likely as a Cup Final pairing (just a 0.20% of happening, in fact), but perhaps that changes down the road!

New York Islanders at Minnesota Wild

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -192, O/U: 5.5

Speaking of superstars delivering the goods, Kirill Kaprizov is one big night away from setting an NHL record for goals scored in a single month of October. The current record is 16 (achieved twice by Mario Lemieux), and Kaprizov enters this contest with 14. This will be his last chance, however, as the Wild won't play against until Sunday.

Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer set an NHL record on Tuesday, playing all five minutes of the overtime period in the Isles' win over Nashville. The 2025 No. 1 overall pick is fourth in average ice time this season, skating 26:43 per game, behind Buffalo's Owen Power, Columbus' Zach Werenski ... and Minnesota's Quinn Hughes.

Buffalo Sabres at Anaheim Ducks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+/Disney+/Hulu) | BUF -130, O/U: 6.5

It felt like the Sabres' Tuesday game against the Sharks would be a high-scoring shootout; instead, it was a 2-0 win for Buffalo. Maybe the hockey gods will reward us Thursday instead?

As a team, the Ducks are allowing 3.58 goals per game, the fourth most this season, while the Sabres are allowing 3.33, the ninth most. So the stage is set for the offense to take flight.

If anyone is "due," it's Tage Thompson, who has just five goals and five assists through 12 games after 40 and 41, respectively last season.

Ottawa Senators at Los Angeles Kings

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | LA -110, O/U: 5.5

After winning five of their first six this season, the Sens have been alternating wins and losses game by game. If that trend continues, Sens fans should expect another W following a 4-1 loss to Vegas on Tuesday. This is the first of their three games played at the California teams, with San Jose on the docket Saturday and Anaheim on Sunday.

The Kings have been on the opposite track in 2026-27; after losing their first six games, L.A. has won three of its last five.

Vancouver Canucks at San Jose Sharks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN) | SJ -198, O/U: 6.5

Neither of these teams has had the start they expected. Yes, the Canucks were anticipated to be not-so-good as they traverse a rebuild, but being on pace for 42 points in the standings is not encouraging! On the positive side, Elias Pettersson appears to have gotten some of his scoring swagger back.

Meanwhile, the Sharks were widely thought of as a playoff team this spring, but 84 points ain't gonna cut it, and that's their current pace. Taking care of business against overmatched opponents is important in racking up W's, so this contest could be a telling one for Macklin Celebrini & Co.

Reminder: Fans can catch all the action in the NHL streaming hub and on the ESPN App.

stories.headline: Sergio Pérez's F1 second act: Red Bull regrets, redemption and a fresh start at Cadillac
stories.summary: Sergio Pérez reflects on his Red Bull exit, finding happiness beyond F1 and rediscovering his love of racing as he prepares for his 300th grand prix.
stories.body:
Sergio Pérez had to leave Formula 1 and come back again to realise there's more to life than just racing. Now he's got his retirement home office all sorted for whenever he walks away a second time.

It's a proper office, Pérez assures ESPN, complete with a desk, a busy calendar and plenty of business to attend to. He has investments to oversee, projects to develop and a charitable foundation to run. He's certainly not short of things to keep himself occupied.

There is, for now, the small matter of finishing his Formula 1 career his own way.

On Sunday Pérez, who returned this year with the upstart Cadillac team, will celebrate his 300th grand prix in front of his adoring crowd in Mexico City, a place which returned to the F1 schedule in 2015 largely due to his superstar status at home. It's a remarkable milestone borne out of fluke and one made more remarkable by the fact that not long ago it seemed his career was done for good.

- Nate Saunders on the contradictions of Austin's COTA

- How Kimi Antonelli can win the title in Mexico City

- Fernando Alonso slams 'low quality bottom third of the grid'

Worst of all, it looked like Pérez's career had ended with the bitter taste of not being on his own terms. His four years as Max Verstappen's teammate at Red Bull -- the toughest gig on the grid -- had delivered race victories and a runner-up finish in the championship, but a promising start to 2024 gave way to a prolonged slump. By the end of the season, he was out of a drive.

In hindsight, getting through that stint of his career now is a remarkable thing.

"I'm amazed at how I did it," Pérez tells ESPN. "I don't think there are many drivers in Formula 1 who could survive that amount of challenge, I'm extremely proud of how I handled myself, in the car, out of the car, mentally, like everything I went through.

"I'm extremely proud of that period, because it was not just about driving the car, it was a lot of things, and that's really it," he adds, referencing the difficult days of 2024.

Red Bull has undergone a lot of change since he left there. Pérez's old team boss Christian Horner and the company's long-time racing advisor Helmut Marko, who famously squabbled over driver decisions for years, both left the team the following year.

"I always knew that the Red Bull period was a very special one, you know, because of all the circumstances there, I never had the opportunity to really show my proper talent there, just because how the team operates."

Pérez's year on the sidelines in 2025 and return with the upstart Cadillac team this year provided that opportunity. The Mexican driver has impressed at the struggling backmarker outfit with strong qualifying and race pace since the beginning of the season and he now has a contract to be with the team until the end of 2029. While he wanted to remind fans who the real Sergio Pérez was, he admits he had to remind himself too.

"I came back because I enjoyed a lot the racing aspect, but I had a lot of points to prove to myself, you know, like, the way I left Red Bull, I knew that it was not fair to my speed."

The 36-year-old has dismissed the notion of racing into his forties like Fernando Alonso, who will turn 46 racing for Aston Martin next season, but he's clearly not ready to walk away just yet.

Though Pérez's career has not seen him join the likes of Alonso and former teammate Verstappen as world champions, he can boast three pole positions, six wins and, as of Sunday, a triple century of race starts. That will see him move into seventh on the all-time list, overtaking Sebastian Vettel's 299. Even if he can't boast the world titles of an Alonso or Vettel, he now views all of it through a very different lens.

"There are so many drivers around the world that would dream to have the career I've had, so it's like everything in life, you always want more, but I think you have to be happy with what you have," Pérez said. "Obviously, I would have liked to be a world champion, you know, by now, but, it depends on a lot of factors. Unfortunately, Formula 1 is not just dependent on your speed and your talent, it depends on having the right surroundings, having the right support around you and all of that, and unfortunately I never had the chance in my career to be a world champion."

Dad time and a home office

Pérez's year out gave him the chance to live a life removed from the grid.

It gave him the chance to spend time with his children. He is one of just four dads on the Formula 1 grid -- former teammate Verstappen, Alonso and Nico Hülkenberg are the others.

"They have some catching up to do! I have four," he joked. Being a dad and having time to properly spend with them, away from the gruelling schedule of an F1 race season, was one of the things he repeatedly reflected on when unveiled as a Cadillac driver at the start of the season.

Clearly, it has given Pérez a grounding not many other drivers have.

"It's when life gets so much better. You realise what you work for. You have all this responsibility next to you. This is the biggest victory a human can have, to have kids, for me it's the most special. I respect people who don't want to have kids, everyone finds their happiness the way they have to, the most important thing is their happiness, but for me it's the biggest thing in life, having kids."

In his year away from F1, Pérez could finally be properly focused on family life.

When asked by ESPN if it's a proper home office set-up, he laughs.

"Yeah, it's a proper office." It's a funny mental image and a long way removed from life at 300 km/h. An F1 driver, usually squeezed inside the cockpit, visor down, focused on the road ahead, instead sat in a nice quiet office environment, working through emails on a laptop with a coffee on the desk.

"It's a bit like that," he laughs. "When I'm not racing, I'm properly into my things, into my businesses, I enjoy that, I love it. I have my office where I look at things, at my schedule, at the calendars. I do very little related to racing though."

"I like business, I like to run my things, my family office, looking for new opportunities, I get involved a lot. I love my foundation, doing things for charity. I love looking for new projects, meeting the right people, hiring good people, all of that, you know, I have a passion for that."

Pérez is also passionate about his charitable work through the Fundación Checo Pérez, which supports disadvantaged children across Mexico through educational programmes, healthcare initiatives and improvements to children's homes. More than anything else, Pérez wants to give back to the country which will welcome him back as a returning hero this weekend.

"I want to push a lot in Mexico, to bring a lot of capital into my country. I believe there's a massive opportunity there, being involved with some good brands, I would like to carry on with some of the great brands I've worked with, do a lot more for my foundation as well."

The milestone race

You wouldn't know Pérez has never won a world championship if you've ever been around him before a grand prix in Mexico. His status at home is legendary and it was even before he claimed an overdue first race victory for Racing Point at the 2020 Sakhir Grand Prix, the one which earned him the move to Red Bull the following season. At home, he's always been revered.

His podiums at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriquez in 2021 and 2022 were high points, but his 2024 visit -- which could so easily have been his last -- the lowest. He qualified 18th and then languished a lap down at the finish, a result which seemed to perfectly sum up his whole situation at Red Bull at the time. Even if he now returns with a backmarking team, he gets a chance to do it over again.

"Just having that moment back again, with all the fans ... it will be very special. Because at one stage it was like, 'we probably won't see this again ever,' you know? And it didn't end the right way. But all of a sudden we've managed to come back and they've been really supportive of me and the team."

The milestone itself only crystallised late due to world events. Coming into the season, it was due to be his 301st. The cancellation of Bahrain and Saudi Arabia's races at the start of the year due to the Iran war then meant it was due to be his 299th, but Bahrain's deal to hold its race in Malaysia a month before Mexico City's event knocked it into the perfect 300 mark. "It couldn't really be any better, you know?" he said, smiling. "To be able to celebrate my 300th race in front of my family, friends, fans and all the sponsors that have supported me."

Pérez's new deal means he should have more opportunities to race in front of his home crowd in Mexico City. But whenever he does decide to walk away, Perez finally seems to be at peace with what comes next.
